chunks: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar al-Jumar al-Ju'fi, who said:
I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I long for al-Ghari.' He said, 'What is your longing for it?'

I said to him, 'I love to visit the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him).' He said, 'Do you know the virtue of visiting him?' I said, 'No, O son of the Messenger of Allah, unless you inform me of that.'
He said, 'When you visit the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), know that you are visiting the bones of Adam, the body of Noah, and the physique of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him).'
I said, 'Indeed, Adam (peace be upon him) descended in Serandib (Sri Lanka) in the east, and they claim that his bones are in the Sacred House of Allah (Mecca). How did his bones come to be in Kufa?'

He said, 'Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Majestic, revealed to Noah (peace be upon him) while he was in the ship that he should circumambulate the House seven times. So he circumambulated the House as Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him.

Then he descended into the water up to his knees and extracted a chest containing the bones of Adam (peace be upon him), so he carried it in the belly of the ship until he circumambulated as Allah willed.
Then he arrived at the gate of Kufa, in the middle of its mosque. Therein, Allah, the Exalted, said to the earth, 'Swallow your water.'
So it swallowed its water from the mosque of Kufa, just as the water began from it, and the crowd that was with Noah (peace be upon him) in the ship dispersed.

So Noah (peace be upon him) took the chest and buried it in al-Ghari, which is a piece of the mountain upon which Allah spoke to Moses with direct speech, and upon which Jesus sanctified, and upon which He took Abraham as a friend, and took Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as a beloved, and made it a dwelling for the prophets.
By Allah, none dwelt in it after his two pure fathers, Adam and Noah, who is more noble than the Commander of the Faithful, may the prayers of Allah be upon him.
So when you visit the side of al-Najaf, visit the bones of Adam, the body of Noah, and the physique of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him).

For indeed you are visiting the first fathers, and Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets, and Ali, the Master of the Successors. And indeed, for his visitor, the gates of heaven are opened at his supplication, so do not be negligent of good.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin (Commander of the Faithful), a title for Imam Ali.
key_terms.التَّابُوتَ: The chest/ark, in which Noah carried Adam's bones.
key_terms.الْغَرِيِّ: Al-Ghari (The Marsh/Region), referring to the area in Kufa where Imam Ali is buried.
key_terms.بَدَنَ نُوحٍ: The body of Noah, believed to be buried in Kufa.
key_terms.جَانِبَ النَّجَفِ: The side of al-Najaf, the area adjacent to the shrine.
key_terms.خَاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ: Khatam al-Nabiyyin (Seal of the Prophets), referring to Prophet Muhammad.
key_terms.عِظَامَ آدَمَ: The bones of Adam, believed to be buried in Kufa.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of visiting the shrine of Imam Ali in Kufa according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the theological significance of al-Ghari (Najaf) as a sacred resting place for primordial prophets, linking the physical act of Ziyarah to the veneration of the 'first' and 'last' prophets. It highlights the unique status of Imam Ali by asserting that no one more noble than him dwells there after Adam and Noah, thereby elevating the shrine to a central locus of Shia spiritual geography and intercessory prayer.
